text:
maria (Support): heads-up — escalation from AcmeCorp. They reported a sudden p95/p99 latency regression on text-generation since we rolled the new quantization profile last night (int8 + fp8 fallbacks). Symptoms: p95 from ~180ms -> ~650ms, p99 bursts up to 1.2s for short-chat requests. Customer impact: high error/backpressure on their fast-path endpoints. Request ids attached: req_az12, req_az13, req_az14.

jason (SRE): thanks — can you paste the model variant and exact config they hit? also which region and whether they were on Hosted vs Dedicated?

maria (Support): they are on Hosted (us-east1) using model redwood-7b-v2 with our new quant profile "q-profile-2026-03" (int8 primary, fp8 experimental fallback, auto-calibration enabled). They did a few runs with concurrency 8, batch_limit 4.

liam (Eng Runtime): pinging eng-runtime. From the rollout notes: q-profile-2026-03 enabled kernel_fp8_path and changed per-layer calibration thresholds (lowered threshold for using int8). Could be a slow path introduced in the fp8 fallback or a calibration mismatch.

anya (ML Infra): possible cause: auto-calibration fallback is currently synchronous during the first few requests after deployment for some workloads — that can add 100-400ms per request if the sample set triggers re-calibration. Also saw an issue in the last run where the fp8 compile path forced a JIT kernel selection that deoptimizes batching for short-seqs.

maria (Support): customer reports spikes even after warm-up (we saw p95 remain high for >10 minutes). They tried repeating identical prompts and saw non-deterministic latency.

liam (Eng Runtime): can you pull the trace for req_az12? I'm looking for where the time is spent -- tokenizer, kv cache, compile/dispatch, or kernel exec. Suggested command: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal.redwood/api/traces?req_id=req_az12" | jq .timeline
```

support-bot: trace req_az12: kernel_compile: 0.02s, dispatch_queue: 0.01s, exec_total: 0.58s, kv_lookup: 0.03s, postproc: 0.04s.

jason (SRE): exec_total 0.58s is suspicious for a short sequence. Compare to baseline: previous stable exec_total ~0.12-0.18s. Looks like an execution kernel path regression.

anya (ML Infra): that matches a known fp8 kernel path that falls back to a slower reference path for some layer shapes when quantization mismatch occurs. I flagged it in the fp8 runtime PR but it slipped through canary.

liam (Eng Runtime): immediate mitigation options: 1) toggle fp8 fallback off for q-profile-2026-03 (force fp16 fallback), 2) revert q-profile for hosted until we push a patched kernel, 3) route AcmeCorp to a compatible model variant pinned to fp16. Which should we do?

maria (Support): customer wants minimal disruption but needs latency back to baseline asap. They prefer a config toggle on their tenant if possible.

jason (SRE): short-term: switch their tenant to fallback_fp16 and disable auto-calibration for that profile. That should be non-disruptive and low-risk. I'll prepare a config patch and a scoped rollout.

liam (Eng Runtime): I'll add a safety toggle to the serving control plane: 
```
PATCH /admin/tenants/acmecorp/config
{
  "q_profile_override": "q-profile-2026-03-fp16-fallback",
  "auto_calibration": false
}
```
Do we have an audit-safe way to apply that for only AcmeCorp?

jason (SRE): yes — we can apply via tenant-level config. I'll schedule the immediate patch and monitor p95.

maria (Support): on it — telling customer we'll toggle their fallback to fp16 and keep them posted. ETA 10m.

support-bot: config patch applied for tenant=AcmeCorp by jason at 1992345880. Monitoring stream subscribed.

anya (ML Infra): follow-up investigation notes: the calibration set used in q-profile-2026-03 was too small and didn't exercise mid-layer activations; when batch-size is small or sequence lengths are short, some layers picked fp8 with no optimized kernel and used a fallback slow path. Fix path: expand calibration corpus and adjust threshold to prefer int8 for those shapes, and landing a faster fp8 kernel for degenerate shapes. We'll produce a patched q-profile (q-profile-2026-03a) and validate on canary.

liam (Eng Runtime): engineering action items:
- Roll back fp8 kernel selection in runtime flags for hosted until patch (liam)
- Add time-based cache for calibration results to avoid synchronous recalibration per-request (liam + anya)
- Add telemetry to surface when kernel falls back to reference slow path (jason)

jason (SRE): monitoring update: after applying fp16 fallback, AcmeCorp p95 dropped from 650ms -> 170ms within 2 minutes. p99 also back to ~230ms. Confirmed by sampling req_az15-az17.

maria (Support): customer notified and pleased. They asked for a postmortem and timeline and want assurance this won't reoccur.

anya (ML Infra): we'll run larger calibration sweep against production-ish traffic patterns and create a canary run across 5% of hosted traffic. Will share evaluation metrics (latency delta, token-level quality regression tests).

liam (Eng Runtime): note: we need to ensure that compile-time kernel selection is idempotent in presence of mixed quant types; adding a defensive check in dispatch to prefer faster known-good kernels when latency SLOs are at risk.

maria (Support): action owner list for customer-facing PM/sales follow-up:
- RCA draft (anya)
- Timeline + rollback summary (liam)
- Customer comms + patch notes (maria)

jason (SRE): closing note: if any of you need me to temporarily route more tenants off the new q-profile, say the word; we've got a hotfix path.

maria (Support): thanks all — keeping thread open for the RCA. I'll update AcmeCorp once we have the RCA draft. :thumbsup:
